blocks.source: The process of finding the derivative of a function is called *differentiation*. From the previous chapter you may have the impression that this process is usually laborious, requires recourse to the definition of the derivative, and depends upon successfully recognizing some limit. It is true that such a procedure is often the only possible approach—if you forget the definition of the derivative you are likely to be lost. Nevertheless, in this chapter we will learn to differentiate a large number of functions, without the necessity of even recalling the definition. A few theorems will provide a mechanical process for differentiating a large class of functions, which are formed from a few simple functions by the process of addition, multiplication, division, and composition. This description should suggest what theorems will be proved. We will first find the derivative of a few simple functions, and then prove theorems about the sum, products, quotients, and compositions of differentiable functions. The first theorem is merely a formal recognition of a computation carried out in the previous chapter.
blocks.translation: 求出一个函数的导函数的过程，称为*求导*。读过上一章，你可能觉得这个过程通常很费力，必须求助于导数的定义，而且能否成功取决于能否认出某个极限。这样的过程的确往往是唯一可行的办法——如果忘了导数的定义，你很可能就会迷失方向。不过，在本章中，我们将学会对大量函数求导，甚至不必回想导数的定义。几个定理将给出一种机械化的过程，使我们能够对很大一类函数求导；这些函数是由少数几个简单函数通过加法、乘法、除法和复合构造出来的。这一描述应该已经暗示了我们将证明哪些定理。我们先求出几个简单函数的导函数，然后证明关于可微函数的和、积、商与复合的定理。第一个定理，只是把上一章做过的一项计算正式表述出来。

blocks.source: Prove that if $f^{(n)}(g(a))$ and $g^{(n)}(a)$ both exist, then $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ exists. A little experimentation should convince you that it is unwise to seek a formula for $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$. In order to prove that $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ exists you will therefore have to devise a reasonable assertion about $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ which can be proved by induction. Try something like: “$(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ exists and is a sum of terms each of which is a product of terms of the form $\ldots$ .”
blocks.translation: 证明：如果 $f^{(n)}(g(a))$ 和 $g^{(n)}(a)$ 都存在，那么 $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ 存在。稍作尝试，你就会相信，试图求出 $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ 的公式并不明智。因此，要证明 $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ 存在，你必须构造一个关于 $(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ 的合理断言，并能用归纳法证明它。可以尝试这样的说法：“$(f\circ g)^{(n)}(a)$ 存在，并且是若干项之和，每一项都是形如 $\ldots$ 的各项的乘积。”

blocks.source: This theorem was proved by the French mathematician Rolle, in connection with the problem of approximating roots of polynomials, but the result was not originally stated in terms of derivatives. In fact, Rolle was one of the mathematicians who never accepted the new notions of calculus. This was not such a pigheaded attitude, in view of the fact that for one hundred years no one could define limits in terms that did not verge on the mystic, but on the whole history has been particularly kind to Rolle; his name has become attached to a much more general result, to appear in the next chapter, which forms the basis for the most important theoretical results of calculus.
blocks.translation: 这个定理是法国数学家罗尔在研究多项式根的近似计算问题时证明的，但最初的表述没有使用导数。事实上，罗尔是那些始终没有接受微积分新观念的数学家之一。考虑到整整一百年间，没有人能用不近乎玄学的语言定义极限，这种态度倒也不算特别顽固。不过，总的来说，历史对罗尔格外厚待：他的名字与一个一般得多的结果联系在了一起；下一章将介绍这个结果，它构成了微积分中最重要的理论成果的基础。
